summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with a history of MS, ulcerative colitis, and asthma was admitted with acute left-sided weakness. Initial imaging revealed a large right frontal brain lesion with mass effect, initially suspected to be tumefactive MS, but unresponsive to steroids. A stereotactic brain biopsy confirmed primary CNS B-cell lymphoma. Her hospital course was complicated by a deep vein thrombosis in the left calf, likely secondary pulmonary embolism with pleuritic chest pain, and healthcare-associated pneumonia requiring IV antibiotics. She was treated with high-dose dexamethasone for cerebral edema, methotrexate chemotherapy, and anticoagulation with heparin followed by Lovenox. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic therapy. She improved neurologically, with regained strength and resolution of fever, and was discharged to an extended care facility to complete antibiotics and prepare for readmission for further chemotherapy.
